title: Assignment operators
learningObjectives: Explain assignment operators and use JavaScript values and operators predictably.

understand.concept: Assignment operators store values in variables. The basic = operator assigns a value; compound operators such as +=, -=, *=, and /= combine an operation with assignment. Logical assignment operators include ||=, &&=, and ??= with different short-circuit rules.
understand.whyItMatters: Compound assignment can make updates concise, but the underlying operation should remain clear. Understand whether a logical assignment uses truthiness or nullishness before applying it.
understand.analogy: Assignment places a value into a named variable; compound assignment updates the stored value using an operation.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; JavaScript coercion, equality, and reference semantics follow the language specification.

explain.narrative: The score becomes 15 after +=5, then 30 after *=2.

examples.explanation: The score becomes 15 after +=5, then 30 after *=2.
examples.expectedOutput: The browser console displays the values and results described.

practise.guidedTask: Rewrite a counter using += and -=. Compare ||= with ??= using empty string, zero, null, and undefined.
practise.independentTask: Write a short program using the concept with realistic values. Predict the output before running it and explain any surprising result.
hints: Inspect both value and typeof when needed.
Use explicit conversion and validate its result.
Avoid relying on implicit coercion in security-sensitive logic.

practice.starterCode:
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"><title>Assignment operators</title></head><body>
<script>let score=10;score+=5;score*=2;console.log(score);</script>
</body></html>

<html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"><title>Assignment operators</title></head><body>

options: Adds 5 to score and assigns the result back
questions.answer: Adds 5 to score and assigns the result back
questions.explanation: The compound assignment adds the right-hand value and stores the result in the variable.

questions.prompt: What is a reliable way to understand a value conversion?
options: Inspect the original value, converted value, and conversion result
questions.answer: Inspect the original value, converted value, and conversion result
questions.explanation: Explicitly checking conversion results prevents invalid values from silently entering later calculations.
